chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: Question about the Scrap Iron Jazz Band
summary: Asked about a Scrap Iron Jazz Band, Briggs suggests it was one of the many groups formed by veterans of regimental brass bands who stayed in Europe.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Now, so that Louie Mitchell, he also -- did he record under the name of the Scrap Iron Jazz Band? Does that name mean anything to you at all?
No. I don't think so. We have so many -- was there a trumpet in the band?
I don't know much about it, but I know that such records did exist.
Yeh, well, you see, we had, during after
during, after World War I, you had many members of the brass bands, who formed -- who stayed, different brass bands, I'm not just talking about Jim Europe's outfit.
Many others, 'cause we had also Caucasians, musicians, brass bands who formed, who stayed, and worked with orchestras and different things. So that might be one of them.
I've been asked such questions before, but I couldn't locate him, so I figured it must have been one of the brass bands, 'cause we're all capable of playing dance music, and playing jazz, you see?
